scope: Theorem 2.3 (Ahlberg–Hoffman and the shape theorem) of the manuscript “No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation” (preprints/No-bigeodesics-in-planar-first-passage-percolation-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 212 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f97d87dc82bcee0c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 5-6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are a deterministic norm m on R2 and a deterministic closed subset C ⊆ S with the following properties. (i) Almost surely, T(0, x) = m(x) + o(|x|) (|x| → ∞). (ii) Almost surely, simultaneously for all rays p from all lattice vertices, there is a unique ρp ∈ C such that (4) Bp(0, x) = ρp(x) + o(|x|) (|x| → ∞). The limiting directions of p lie in A(ρp). At each vertex the set of realized functionals is C. (iii) For each fixed ρ ∈ C, almost surely there is exactly one ray gρ(x) with functional ρ from each x ∈ Z2. These rays coalesce. Their family is backwards finite: for each vertex z, the set of x for which gρ(x) contains z is finite. 6 OPENAI The norm m and the set C have the rotation and reflection symmetries of the square lattice.
